Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.

description.text: The average Adshawman grows up hunting wild beasts, felling the titanic trees that loom over our realm, and lugging great trunks to sawmills. Our people possess a great strength and sturdiness because of this bucolic upbringing, rumoured to rival that of even an orc.
description.text_en: The average Adshawman grows up hunting wild beasts, felling the titanic trees that loom over our realm, and lugging great trunks to sawmills. Our people possess a great strength and sturdiness because of this bucolic upbringing, rumoured to rival that of even an orc.

description.text: Before the knife-eared bastards of Celmaldor incited our subjects to rebel, and before those pesky Blue Reachmen had a notion of independence, the Kingdom of Adshaw ruled over much of the western Alenic Reach, reining in the notoriously rebellious Reachmen and their cities, and establishing a realm powerful enough to withstand the Kingdom of Gawed itself. Even if we may have fallen far from such glory, all remember when the banner of Rygan flew across the Serpentshead.

description.text: Our lands have a great lack of good stone to build forts out of, therefore the majority of our bastions are primarily constructed out of Greatwood Oak, of which we have plenty of to repair any damages.

description.text: Adshaw was founded by the great chieftain of the Adderic tribe, Rygan of Adderwood. The Adshaw dynasty has always and will always rule this realm, through all her glory and tribulations, forging a sense of unity and brotherhood amongst the once rivalled tribes of the northern Greatwoods.
description.text_en: Adshaw was founded by the great chieftain of the Adderic tribe, Rygan of Adderwood. The Adshaw dynasty has always and will always rule this realm, through all her glory and tribulations, forging a sense of unity and brotherhood amongst the once rivalled tribes of the northern Greatwoods.

description.text: The Ambush at Coldmarket in 1024 marked the end of the Kingdom of Adshaw. While marching to finally quell the last remnants of the Blue Reachmen Wars of Independence in Coldmarket, King Rylen of Adshaw's forces were ambushed by a secret coalition of rotten elves from Celmaldor and Blue Reachmen separatists. We were used to the tactics of the Blue Reachmen, yes, but the elven-eyed archers overwhelmed our forces and led to their shattering when an arrow met with our king. Since then, we've developed several tactics and formations to avoid such a disaster from happening again.

description.text: Since the days of Rygan and the dozen tribes of the Greatwoods, every able man has been required to keep themselves and their weapons in good shape, and be fully prepared to take up arms in the name of his lord and sovereign.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you dislike espionage and diplomatic prerequisites and want to advance smoothly by declaring wars alone.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Build spy networks, assassinate target rulers, install your dynasty and subject neighbouring Reach states. Agents, noble revolts and protection agreements connect diplomatic manoeuvring directly to expansion. The outcome of the Clovibian campaign changes later missions and the dual-kingdom narrative; it is not a self-selected good-or-evil ending.
player_overview.overview: Adshaw's appeal is that it turns the spy network, usually used to fabricate claims, into a real political weapon. Rather than overwhelming the world with a spectacular mage or a unique piece of artificery, you cultivate relationships among the Reach states and create fractures, making other people's thrones, nobles and protection agreements serve your interests. In time, the small state's intrigues can reshape the northern order. Players who enjoy setting the pieces before closing the net are more likely to enjoy it than those who only want to fight one major war after another.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy espionage, diplomacy, subjects and political manoeuvring in the north.
signature_features: Build a spy network, assassinate a target ruler, install your dynasty and subject neighbouring Reach states.
Agents, noble revolts and protection agreements make diplomacy an immediate part of expansion.
The outcome of the Clovibian campaign changes later missions and the dual-kingdom narrative, rather than offering a self-selected good-or-evil ending.
player_overview.tagline: A court operator who turns spy networks into dynasties, subjects and a northern sphere of influence.

reasons: Build spy networks, assassinate target rulers, install your dynasty and subject neighbouring Reach states.
Agents, noble revolts and protection agreements connect diplomacy directly to expansion.
The Clovibian campaign outcome changes later missions and the dual-kingdom narrative, rather than creating a self-selected moral route.
warnings: Espionage and diplomatic prerequisites are frequent; repeatedly declaring wars is not enough to make progress smooth.
Assassination, agitation and indirect rule occur; a protection agreement should not automatically be read as voluntary.
The Clovibian line advances according to campaign state, so the same story is not guaranteed every time.

positive_indicators: Investment in ports, cities and northern governance.
A conditional narrative of cooperation with the Frozenmaw frontier.
values.rationale: Espionage missions directly kill foreign rulers, install proxy dynasties and impose subject status; agents also incite noble revolts, reducing dignity and restraint. Urban development and northern reorganisation provide public benefits. Compared with Khozrugan (47), expansionist but without established atrocities, and Corvuria (23), with more severe violations, Adshaw sits on the politically manipulative end of Neutral. Monarchy and conquest are not deductions in themselves. Cooperation with Clovibians is not an optional, wholesale redemption route; no moral branch is invented.
red_flags: Espionage missions kill foreign rulers and install proxy dynasties.
Agents incite revolts to control cities.
